title: Unique counit-compatible isomorphism between right Kan extensions
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be categories [def-nagata-category] in chosen universes, $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $H:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ functors, and $R,S:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ functors with natural transformations $\epsilon:R\circ Q\to H$ and $\eta:S\circ Q\to H$. Suppose both pairs are right Kan extensions of $H$ along $Q$: for every $T:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ and $\theta:T\circ Q\to H$ there is a unique $r:T\to R$ with $\epsilon\circ(rQ)=\theta$, and a unique $s:T\to S$ with $\eta\circ(sQ)=\theta$. Then there is a unique natural isomorphism $u:R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ satisfying $\eta\circ(uQ)=\epsilon$. Its inverse satisfies $\epsilon\circ(u^{-1}Q)=\eta$. No smallness of $\mathcal C$ or existence of other Kan extensions is assumed. Here a functor preserves identities and compositions, a natural transformation $A\to B$ is a family $v_D:A(D)\to B(D)$ commuting with every arrow of $\mathcal D$, and a natural isomorphism is a natural transformation whose components are all invertible.
